metadata.why_the_path_matters: W-0043. The path, the status and the body shape all come from the Target V1 contract, which is what TargetV1CallbackTransport actually speaks. The first version of this stub matched /v1/orders/.*/ivr-result and answered 202 with {response_code, accepted}: three independent mismatches, so the stack answered 404 to every real callback. Nothing caught it because the compose smoke only asked whether the containers were healthy.
metadata.why_the_echo_matters: callback_id and correlation_id are ECHOED, not canned. The transport compares both against the outbox row and reports CALLBACK_ACK_INVALID when either differs, so a fake returning constants would be rejected. The echo is what makes this a round trip rather than a stubbed 200.
